A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MM-SHAP/CC-SHAP study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original accuracy, modality-contribution and explanation self-consistency results for three VLMs, including Tables 1–3 and appendix case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and adds results for mPLUG-Owl3 across the existing benchmarks and SHAP measures.

M1.justification: The proposed normalization, aggregation and modality-comparison pipeline remains unchanged. Equation 2 is corrected to average normalized contributions, matching the pipeline already illustrated in v2; this establishes a mathematical correction, not a redesigned algorithm. mPLUG-Owl3 is an evaluated model.

E1.justification: Both versions use VQA, GQA, balanced GQA, MSCOCO, FoilIt and the same VALSE instruments and task formulations. Video appears in the description of mPLUG-Owl3's prior training, not as newly evaluated data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The model comparisons in Tables 1–3 and Figure 1 gain mPLUG-Owl3. The three original VLMs and encoder reference comparisons remain. The six edit-based comparison tests remain available for the original models but are not evaluated on mPLUG-Owl3.

E3.justification: v3 adds a 7B mPLUG-Owl3 evaluation configuration and explicitly restricts its self-consistency evaluation to CC-SHAP because of implementation and time constraints. Existing prompts, metrics, full-VALSE evaluations and 100-sample SHAP evaluations remain unchanged; revised accuracies do not establish an undocumented protocol change.

E4.justification: The answer-versus-post-hoc/CoT analysis extends to mPLUG-Owl3, adding evidence of a smaller modality-contribution shift and more stable CoT accuracy in Section 4.4 and Tables 2–3. The six edit-based robustness tests and their retained-model results are unchanged, as are the individual case studies in Tables 4–11.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations over three runs for representative VQA and existence experiments, plus the same table-level summaries. v3 extends this reporting to mPLUG-Owl3. Its new 'statistically significant' wording supplies no newly specified test, p-value or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: mPLUG-Owl3 adds leading Table 1 results of 88% pairwise accuracy and 76% alignment accuracy, and positive average VALSE CC-SHAP scores. Existing results also change substantially: Table 3 mean CoT accuracies for BakLLaVA/LV-Mistral/LV-Vicuna change from 59/57/60% to 80/81/68%. Table 2 revises several accuracies too. These are reported numerical revisions; their cause is not explained.

T1.justification: Equation 2 changes from averaging raw Shapley values to normalized contribution ratios, resolving its inconsistency with the illustrated pipeline. New Appendices B.1–B.2 formalize Shapley values, fairness properties and CC-SHAP. However, Equation 5's newly supplied normalizer is inconsistent with the efficiency property stated in Equation 6.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion narrow the claim that VLMs are less self-consistent than LLMs to 'most tested VLMs,' accommodating mPLUG-Owl3. The central claims about text dominance and increased image contribution during explanation generation remain.

C2.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 newly interpret mPLUG-Owl3's behavior through reduced linguistic bias, a smaller modality gap and possible benefits from broader/video training. Section 2 expands the critique of edit-based tests, including semantic-evaluation errors and search-dependent outcomes. Most existing limitations are retained in Appendix A.

D1.justification: v2 promises a future code release; v3 states that code is available and supplies a repository address. v3 also provides the mPLUG-Owl3 checkpoint address and documents coalition subsampling and the cosine-distance formulation of CC-SHAP. These are access and methodological disclosures, not demonstrated implementation changes.

R1.justification: v3 acknowledges Dogan et al. (2024) as concurrent VALSE research and adds Ye et al. (2024), Shapley (1953), and Lundberg and Lee (2017). Meister et al. (2022) and Garcia et al. (2023) disappear with the ethics statement. The central positioning relative to MM-SHAP and CC-SHAP remains.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites expand the introduction and test explanations, often replace 'prediction' with 'answer,' and restructure model and metric descriptions into lists. Limitations move to Appendix A, mathematical background and acknowledgements are added, and the ethics statement is removed. The main Sections 1–5 retain their narrative order.

P2.justification: The document switches from two-column to single-column layout, extensively resizes and relocates displays, and swaps the two method schematics' order. Figures 1, 4, 5, 7 and 8 and Tables 1–3 accommodate the fourth model. Table captions still incorrectly say three models, and captions for Tables 7 and 11 now overlap page-number areas.

improvement.justification: Adding a model outside the original LLaVA family exposes an important exception and leads to more appropriately qualified self-consistency claims. Correcting Equation 2 and supplying code-access information also improve clarity and reproducibility. These gains are limited by unexplained substantial accuracy revisions, the new Shapley-normalizer inconsistency, and presentation defects; they support a modest overall improvement rather than a major one.
